title: feat(multiaxis): the Rotary Flow multi-band and single-helix kernel
body:
﻿## What changed

The picked Rotary Flow guide chains now read as ONE ordered set. The
chain-set law lives in a new `rotary_flow_set` module of the motion
crate; the band loop of `rotary_flow` gains the shared-boundary dedup,
the single-chain lap, the sense normalization, and the set refusals.

- **Multi-band.** Three or more ordered chains machine one band per
  adjacent pair, and the SHARED boundary chain is cut once: band k > 0
  starts at its first interior pass. Band k - 1's last pass already
  walked the shared chain at the same stations, the same push-out and
  the same climb setting, so nothing is lost.
- **Single helical chain.** A lone chain machines the full revolution:
  the kernel synthesizes the second boundary as the chain's own next
  lap, one whole turn on in the unwrap's own theta (`th + TAU`), every
  other coordinate held. The lap takes no whole-turn alignment (it is
  exact by construction). The lap's two edges are the SAME world curve,
  so the closing pass is dropped - the picked chain emits once.
- **Sense normalization.** A chain wound against its pair is walked
  backwards, said in the notes. This supersedes #2824's opposite-sense
  refusal: the feature layer reads a chain's direction from the mesh,
  never from the pick, so the refusal fired on legal picks the user
  could not reverse (the probe on the bar showed the end-face rings
  extracting wound -TAU while the profile rings extract +TAU). The raw
  pairing of two oppositely wound chains twists the band a whole turn;
  the reversal untwists it. Review rework (PR #4018 review, item 1):
  the normalization now runs ONCE over the complete ordered set
  before any band is cut (`normalize_set`), and the SAME normalized
  guide bounds both adjacent bands - never a per-band copy, which
  left the next band's lower boundary at the raw winding and flipped
  the second band's cutting direction without a change to climb.
- **Ring lap guard.** Review rework (item 2): a single guide that
  turns about the axis at one axial station and one radius - a closed
  ring or an open arc of one - is refused by name before a pass is
  generated (`refuse_ring_lap`): its lap reads a positive angular
  width but sweeps no band area, and the pass family would repeat one
  closed cut. A guide that advances in station or in radius sweeps a
  real band and passes.
- **Refusals, all by name.** Chains that meet or cross are refused at
  the shared spot (the exact segment-pair law, Ericson 5.1, at the
  corner-lattice dust). Consecutive bands whose mean developed offsets
  oppose (dot < 0) are refused as a set out of band order. A
  perpendicular turn is not a doubling back: bands may tile around a
  corner. Zero-length, non-finite and duplicate chains keep the #2824
  refusals.

## Geometry readings

- The lap's developed width is exactly `R_ref * TAU` at the chain's own
  outermost radius: `dth = TAU` and `dv = 0` at every matched place, so
  `cross_width` reads one full revolution. The pass count divides it at
  the stepover, and the emitted count is `ceil(width / step)` - the
  closing pass is the picked chain itself.
- The multi-band dedup emits `count_0 + count_k - (k)` passes over k
  bands: band k > 0 takes `count - 1`, and the first interior pass sits
  one stepover or less from the shared boundary, so the coverage never
  opens a gap.
- Refusal readings: the meet test is the exact segment-pair closest
  distance (four endpoint candidates plus the clamped interior solve,
  Ericson 5.1 as the guard cites it); the backtrack test compares the
  mean developed offsets of consecutive pairs and refuses only a
  strictly negative dot.

## Pins

- Motion, `tests/rotary_flow/bands.rs`: three ordered root helices cut
  two bands in 7 passes (4 + 4 - 1) with pairwise-distinct landings;
  one root helix covers the full revolution in 26 passes, the first
  pass winding exactly `TAU`, gouge-free per the station pin; a ring
  that crosses a corner chain refuses at the crossing's own spot.
  Review rework pins: the middle pick reversed holds the direction
  of every pass of every band for BOTH climb settings (aligned
  control and mixed winding, pass by pass); a single closed ring
  refuses the zero-area lap family by name; a single open ring arc
  refuses the same.
- Motion, unit: the lap morph, the meet law with its witness, the
  backtrack law, the pass-count law, the backward walk (twice is the
  identity, the knots stay ascending), the set normalization (mixed
  winding resolved once, the cascade judged against the normalized
  neighbour), the ring lap guard (a ring refuses, a helix and a
  radial arc pass).
- App, `tests/rotary_flow_band.rs`: three ring chains cut two bands,
  the plunge count agrees with the bands' own stated counts, no two
  passes land on one station, the notes state the shared boundary and
  the sense walk.
- App, `tests/rotary_flow_lap.rs` (new file; reason below): one
  meridian chain machines the full revolution in 19 passes, one
  landing per azimuth, lap note stated; the meridian-plus-ring set
  refuses at the shared corner, with no path cached.

## What was not exercised

- The app-level pins run on the turned bar, not a helical screw: the
  app's slicing refuses open meshes, and a closed screw fixture with
  sharp helical edges is its own fixture work. The helical single-chain
  and multi-band coverage is pinned at the motion level on the groove
  fixture (one-turn and three-turn rotors, station and swept-ball
  proofs).
- The heavy lanes are not run (#3556: no PR gets the full heavy lanes;
  this is a P7 under the safety floor, so no targeted heavy step is
  owed). The light lane ran partially green (motion light: lib, the
  adaptive troch twins, app light: pocket_pass_start); its
  all-binaries release build step failed on machine disk during the
  run, not on code - the same build passed clean after a full rebuild
  of the touched crates.
- No example catalog case exercises Rotary Flow, so their outputs
  cannot change; the quick plan still ran all three catalog suites,
  green.
- The quick gate's app prebuild wedged once (#3675) and the app suites
  were run one by one instead: all 20 planned suites green, clippy
  `-D warnings` clean on both touched crates.
- Review rework head (99283bc76, after the merge of main 49bfcaea8):
  the rework gate ran `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` (683
  passed, 0 failed, 22 ignored), `cargo test -p camcraft-motion
  --test rotary_flow` (14 passed, 1 heavy-ignored), `cargo test -p
  camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_band` (7 passed), `cargo test -p
  camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_lap` (2 passed), the three new
  tests by name, and clippy `-D warnings` clean on
  `camcraft-motion --all-targets` and on the touched
  `camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_band` binary. The light lane of
  the first head stands; the rework diff touches only the flow
  kernel and its own pins, and the review re-runs what it needs.
- The crossing between NON-adjacent guides that the review named
  non-blocking (pre-existing on main) is filed as #4032 and stays
  out of this branch.

## File note (#3187)

`crates/app/tests/rotary_flow_lap.rs` is a new top-level test file: the
rotary domain keeps one top-level file per topic, and a second file
holds these laws so `rotary_flow_band.rs` stays under the 400-line
ceiling.

## Changelog

Rotary Flow: three or more ordered guide chains machine one band per
adjacent pair with the shared boundary cut once; a single guide chain
machines the full revolution as its own next lap; the complete set is
wound one way before the bands are cut, so a reversed pick never flips
a band's cutting direction; a single ring guide - closed or an open
arc - is refused by name, its lap sweeps no band area; chains that
meet or cross, and sets out of band order, are refused by name.

Fixes #2829

- Collapse interior Clipper lattice micro-steps (`< 5e-5` mm) in `ring_fill::clean_walk` before `share_ends` so segment tangents stay stable on rings and `WALL` loops.

title: fix(sim): a box side a few ulps longer than whole cells gets no extra column
body:
## What changed

One rule for every stock or verdict lattice sized from a length: a side within a relative 1e-9 of a whole number of cells gets that whole number of cells; a real part of a cell still gets its cell.

- `stock_sim::kernel::cells_across(extent, cell)` counts cells across a length.
- `stock_sim::kernel::edge_cells(v, cell, upper)` (new) is the same law for an edge locked to the origin.

Sites on the rule:
- `Dexel::block` (column stock).
- The field box gate and the field cylinder gate (`backend_build.rs`). The cylinder gate counts the circumscribed square the column arm builds.
- The exact carry read `History::read` (`carry_exact.rs`), with `.max(1)`, so a thin box keeps one column.
- The field arm's verdict lattice `lattice_of` (`march.rs`), by `edge_cells`.
- The side-on slabs of a cut body (`carry_side.rs`), with `.max(1)`.
- The mesh stock gate on both arms, `from_facets` (`cut.rs`, `backend_build.rs`), plus the one cell of margin each side.

Left as they are, because they hold no stock and the case cannot arise there: the edge-break window in `wall_anchor.rs` divides by 256 (exact), and the `scan.rs` envelope grid has a full margin of air beyond the part.

## Readings

A 12.7 mm side two ulps long over a 0.254 mm cell:
- Block and exact carry: 50 columns (was 51). No material past the box edge (was up to one cell).
- Field verdict lattice: 50 columns (was 51, against the column arm's 50).
- Side-on carry of a cut body: 50 slabs (was 51).
- Mesh stock on either arm: 52 columns with the margin (was 53). A strip 4094 cells a few ulps long now builds on both arms (was refused as 4097).

## Pinning tests

`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cell_count_tests.rs`, synthetic shapes only, 9 tests:
- `a_whole_number_of_cells_up_to_rounding_is_that_number`
- `no_material_stands_past_a_box_edge_read_a_few_ulps_long`
- `the_cell_ceiling_gate_counts_the_same_columns`
- `the_exact_carry_read_counts_the_blocks_columns`
- `the_field_box_gate_counts_the_same_columns`
- `both_cylinder_gates_count_the_same_columns`
- `the_field_verdict_lattice_over_a_box_has_the_column_arms_columns`
- `the_side_on_carry_slices_a_height_a_few_ulps_over_whole_cells_into_whole_slabs`
- `both_mesh_stock_gates_count_the_same_columns`

Each site set back to its old count turns its test red; with the rule, all 9 pass.

## Gates

On the final head c2dcb516c (upstream/main merged in):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 83 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.6 min).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cell_count_tests`: 9 passed, 0 failed.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes and the light gate (release build of the app).
- The GUI.

## Related

- #4047: a cylinder stock over about 1000 cells across builds on the column arm and is refused on the field arm by the per-facet cell budget in `field_gen.rs`. Measured on main; not changed here.

Effort: high (stock simulation is under the safety floor).
Changelog: Stock: a side a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells no longer gets an extra column, slab or verdict cell, on either backend.

title: fix(tools,sim,ui): read corner_r for dovetail cutters
body:
## What changed

Dovetail cutters (`ToolKind::Dovetail`) now read `corner_r` across geometry, verification, stock simulation, and the UI:

- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `Head::Dove` stores `{ cot, corner_r }`. `Undercut::rho` evaluates the corner arc up to `s_tan = c * (1 + sin t)` and the tangent flank above `s_tan`. `Undercut::contact()` returns `(r, corner_r)`.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `undercut::refusal` checks `corner_r` in `[0, diameter / 2]`, checks `s_tan <= flute_len + NECK_MEETS`, and checks neck clearance against the rounded flank.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs` and `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`: `head_outline` and `Tool::meridian` emit the rounded corner arc and straight flank.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/`: `Cutter::atoms` emits `Prof::Zone` (`[0, s_tan]`) and `Prof::Dove` (`[s_tan, flute_len]`), or a single `Prof::Zone` when the flank top meets `s_tan`. `swept::rho_expanded` and `rotary_geom::shapes` handle `Prof::Zone`. `Frame` moves to `probe_frame.rs` under the 400-line rule.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/`: `SdfTool::Dovetail` and `RevKind::Dove` add `corner: f64`. `field_dove::dove_dist` computes the exact Euclidean SDF of the rounded dovetail head.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`: `tool_settings_grid`, `tool_summary`, `tool_cutter_params`, and `tool_undercut_row::seed` show and preserve `Corner radius` for `ToolKind::Dovetail`, while keeping it hidden and zeroed for `TSlot`, `Keyseat`, and `Lollipop`.
- `docs/decisions/4004-dovetail-corner-radius.md`: records the unattended design decisions.

## Readings

For the `#4004` dovetail cutter (`diameter = 19.05 mm`, `tip_angle = 60 deg`, `flute_len = 9.525 mm`, `shank_d = 8.0 mm`):

- `corner_r = 0.0 mm`: top radius is `4.026 mm` (`contact = (9.525, 0.0)`). The 24 mm wide, 30 deg slot verifies clean and posts.
- `corner_r = 0.254 mm`: top radius is `4.212 mm` (`+0.186 mm` wider; `contact = (9.525, 0.254)`). The 24 mm slot catches `Warning::Gouge` and holds the post.
- `corner_r = 3.0 mm`: top radius is `6.222 mm` (`+2.196 mm` wider; `contact = (9.525, 3.0)`). The 24 mm slot catches `Warning::Gouge` and holds the post, and field stock removes the wider flank and rounded bottom corner.

## Verification

- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass (0 warnings).
- `camcraft-tools` lib tests (`undercut` 15, `meridian` 13, `tool_sanity` 7, `cutter_profile` 4): pass, including `a_rounded_dovetail_reads_its_corner_radius_and_widened_flank` and `a_dovetail_corner_radius_refusals_name_the_rule`.
- `camcraft-sim` lib tests (`verify::probe_meridian_tests` 1, `verify::swept::tests` 2, `stock_sim::field_dove::tests` 2, `stock_sim::field_solid::tests` 3): pass, including `a_lifted_dovetail_corner_zone_is_never_grown_smaller_than_its_solid` and 19,980-sample `the_dovetail_distance_matches_a_dense_boundary_reference`.
- `camcraft-sim` integration tests (`undercut_laws` 16, `verify_avoid_undercut` 4, `undercut_fixture_envelope` 3): pass, including `a_rounded_dovetail_flank_gouges_the_24mm_slot_and_cuts_wider_in_field_stock` and `a_rounded_dovetail_keeps_clearance_on_its_corner_and_flank`.
- `camcraft-motion` tests (`machining2d::undercut` 9, `golden_undercut` 4): pass, including `a_rounded_dovetail_shifts_by_its_widest_corner_and_keeps_z_at_station`.
- `camcraft-app` integration tests (`mcp_slot_undercut` 8, `mcp_undercut_fixture` 3, `stock_play` 8, `stock_play_partial` 4, `tool_gate` 10, `tool_law` 7): pass, including `a_dovetail_corner_radius_catches_the_24mm_slot_gouge_and_holds_the_post`.

title: fix(motion): check trochoidal clean-up engagement with step-down and advisory warning (#3849)
body:
Check 2D and 3D Adaptive (Trochoidal) clean-up passes against the cutter radial engagement limit across every `max_engagement` setting (including the 90.0 deg default).

### Summary of Changes
- **Checked clean-up ladder (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch_clean.rs`, `adaptive_troch.rs`, `adaptive_troch_level.rs`, `machining3d/troch.rs`)**:
  - Factored clean-up peeling into `plan_cleanup_step` and added `plan_cleanup_checked`, which carves a single-level stock with the planned lanes and measures clean-up passes against `t.max_engagement` using `quality::measure` whenever clean-up chains are emitted.
  - When baseline clean-up exceeds `t.max_engagement`, steps down the peel step along `CLEANUP_LADDER` (`1.0, 0.75, 0.5, 0.35, 0.25`) until engagement fits within the limit, noting the reduction on the toolpath.
  - If even the finest ladder step still exceeds `t.max_engagement`, emits a named note via `cleanup_engagement_note` (`CLEANUP_ENGAGEMENT_NOTE_PREFIX`) instead of silently overloading the cutter or dropping the 90.0 deg default check.
  - Wired `plan_cleanup_checked` into both `adaptive_troch.rs` (2D, removing the `max_engagement != DEFAULT_MAX_ENGAGEMENT` skip) and `adaptive_troch_level.rs` / `machining3d/troch.rs` (3D).
- **Advisory operation & status-line warning (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `crates/app/src/warned_moves.rs`, `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, `crates/ui/src/operations.rs`)**:

title: refactor(ui): view cube, marker and axis inks are theme tokens
body:
Stacked on #3992 (which is stacked on #3990). This branch starts from `issue/1120-handle-inks`. Its own commits are 114f7b171 (the change) and eef05252f (the alpha fix of the review). e49b5a20f merges the #3990 and #3992 review fixes into this branch. Review those commits only. Merge #3990 and #3992 first.

## What changed

The second family of #1120: the view cube, marker and axis inks.

- Twelve colour tokens join `Tokens`. Each is also a theme-file key (`colors.<name>`):
  - the view cube and its nav buttons: `cube_edge`, `cube_label`, `cube_glyph_on`, `cube_glyph_off`;
  - the corner hint: `viewport_hint`;
  - the playback tool marker: `marker_stem`, `marker_ring`, `marker_dot`;
  - the axis triad of the Axes button and the handles: `axis_x`, `axis_y`, `axis_z`;
  - the hover gold of the view cube dot and of the machined facet: `viewport_hover`.
- The dark table holds the old dark-ground set of `ground_ink::cube_ink`. The light table holds the old light-ground set. No pixel changes.
- `ground_ink::cube_ink_on(&Tokens, light)` builds the `CubeInk` from a token table. `cube_ink(light)` keeps its signature and reads the built-in table of that ground. The face and button greys stay numbers chosen by the ground.
- `viewcube.rs` and `shell.rs` read `viewport_hover` for the gold.
- The ground rule in `theme_files/overlay.rs`: before this change the cube chose its set by the viewport ground, not by the base. When a theme file makes the ground light on the dark base (or dark on the light base), each of the twelve keys that the file omits takes the value of the built-in table of that ground. A key that the file sets always wins. `docs/user-guide/themes.md` says so.
- The built-in tables write `from_rgba_premultiplied(a, a, a, a)` for the old `from_white_alpha(a)`, because `from_white_alpha` is not `const`. The values are equal (ecolor 0.36.2); the test pins them against `from_white_alpha`.
- The facet veil is `ground_ink::facet_veil(viewport_hover)`. It reads the token unmultiplied, then sets alpha 90. Thus a semi-transparent `viewport_hover` in a theme file keeps its colour (review of this PR: `#FF000080` gave `[45, 0, 0, 90]`, now `[90, 0, 0, 90]`). The built-in gold is opaque and gives the same veil as before.
- The colour-literal guard loses the rows of `ground_ink.rs` and `viewcube.rs`. `shell.rs` goes from 9 to 7. `theme/tables.rs` goes from 38 to 62.
- The example theme and the colour table of the user guide have the twelve keys.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1120-ground-inks.md`.

## Pinning tests

In `crates/ui/tests/theme_files/viewport_inks.rs`, a module of the existing `theme_files` test binary (#3187: no new binary):

- `the_built_in_columns_keep_the_view_cube_and_marker_colours`: each table carries the old literals of its ground.
- `the_view_cube_inks_follow_the_viewport_ground_of_a_theme_file`: the ground rule, in the two directions, with a key that the file sets. This test fails when the rule is removed (checked locally).
- `each_view_cube_ink_is_a_theme_key`: each key sets its own ink.
- `the_facet_veil_keeps_the_hover_colour_of_a_semi_transparent_token`: the built-in gold gives the old veil, and the review probe `#FF000080` gives `[90, 0, 0, 90]`. With the old channel read it fails with `[45, 0, 0, 90]` (checked locally).

Also: `theme_example::example_loads_and_holds_the_dark_defaults` (the example equals `Tokens::DARK`), the existing `viewport_ground_tests` (cube greys and 3:1 contrast on the light ground), and `theme_files::colour_literals::no_colour_literal_outside_the_allowed_rows`.

## Gates

On the head eef05252f:

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 10 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (3.1 min). It includes `ui suites: lib` and `ui suites: theme_files` (28 tests).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches none (0 steps reached).

## Screenshots

The same scenes as #3992: Move mode on the demo Block (move arrows, turn rings, axis balls, view cube) and two picked points, in the dark and light theme. title: test(ui): guard against new colour literals outside the theme tokens
body:
## What changed

This is the first PR for #1120. It adds a guard and changes no colour.

- New guard `crates/ui/tests/theme_files/colour_literals.rs`, with its scanner in `crates/ui/tests/theme_files/colour_scan.rs`. It walks `crates/ui/src` and counts the colour literals in each file that is not a test file (`tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs`, `tests/`). A colour literal is a named constant such as `Color32::WHITE`, or a constructor whose arguments are all numbers written in place, such as `Color32::from_rgb(245, 240, 250)`, also across lines. A constructor over variables (`from_rgb(r, g, b)`) converts a colour chosen elsewhere and does not count. `Color32::TRANSPARENT` does not count. Comments do not count: `//` to the end of the line, also after code, and `/* */`, also nested. The text of a string or char literal is kept as it is.
- Each count must equal its row in `ALLOWED`:
  - a file with a new literal, or a file with no row, fails: "read a theme token instead";
  - a file with fewer literals fails until its row is lowered or removed. Thus the list only shrinks.
- Each row says why:
  - `keep:` for a colour that is not a choice for a theme: the token tables, the contrast maths, and a colour that only measures text;
  - `move (#1120 <family>)` for a site that a later PR moves to theme tokens.
- On `main` at f287a370c the list has 24 files and 142 literals. About 105 of them are sites to move (the 2026-11-12 estimate said 51).
- The guard does not see colour data kept as plain numbers: the G-code syntax table in `gcode_highlight.rs` (tuples) and `[u8; 3]` consts such as `PICK_RGB8`. The family PRs move those by name.
- Test placement (#3187): the guard is two modules of the existing `theme_files` test binary, not a new binary. The `theme_files` gate map now also names `ui::egui_app`, so each UI change runs the guard.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1120-colour-literal-guard.md`.

## The plan after this PR

One PR for each family. Each adds its tokens to `Tokens` (dark and light tables) and to the theme-file keys (`theme_files::COLOR_NAMES`), moves the sites, and lowers its rows. Each is `Refs #1120`. The last one is `Fixes #1120`.

1. Viewport overlays: pick, avoid and handle inks, ground ink, view cube, viewport bar, generate overlay, drop hint, shell overlays.
2. Tool drawings: tool, holder and profile previews, tool library views.
3. Verdict palettes (`colorvision.rs`): into the token table, values unchanged, as the issue says.
4. G-code syntax colours, window chrome and status inks.

## Pinning tests

- `theme_files::colour_literals::no_colour_literal_outside_the_allowed_rows`: the guard. A failure prints today's counts in the row format.
  - With one literal added to `egui_app/error_text.rs`, it fails with `egui_app/error_text.rs: 2 colour literals, the row allows 1: read a theme token instead`.
  - With one `Color32::WHITE` in `egui_app/window_chrome.rs` replaced by `Color32::TRANSPARENT`, it fails with `egui_app/window_chrome.rs: 1 colour literals, the row says 2: lower the row to 1`.
- `theme_files::colour_literals::the_rows_are_sorted_and_each_says_why`.
- `theme_files::colour_scan::the_counter_sees_each_form_and_skips_comments`: the counter on a fixed text, with a constructor split over lines and two conversions of variables that must not count.
- `theme_files::colour_scan::a_comment_after_code_neither_hides_nor_adds_a_literal`: the two probes of the review. `from_rgb(1, // red` then `2, 3)` counts 1, and `let x = 0; // Color32::WHITE` counts 0.
- `theme_files::colour_scan::strings_and_char_literals_keep_their_text`: a `//` in a string and in a raw string, a `'"'` char literal, a lifetime, and a nested block comment.

## Gates

On the head e4b71bb0d (three commits: the guard, the stricter counter, then the review fixes):

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 1 step (`ui suites: theme_files`, 22 tests), 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `rustfmt --check` on the two new modules: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches none (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: 0 steps reached).

## Not exercised

- No change to the app. The guard reads source files only, so the PR has no screenshots.
- A literal written through a `use` alias (for example `use egui::Color32 as C`) is not counted. No such alias is in `crates/ui` today.

title: fix(plasma): Plasma Profile takes a start pick and an exit pick
body:
## What changed

- Plasma Profile takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `Ring` (`KindInfo::pick()`).
- The picks are the operation-level `picks` of #3339 / PR #3871. This PR adds no field, no command and no MCP tool.
- Start pick: the lead-in of the nearest closed contour lands on the projection of the pick on the profile. The pierce is at the start of that lead-in, in the scrap.
- Exit pick: the torch cuts the full contour. Then it cuts on to the projection of the exit pick. The lead-out leaves there and the torch goes off at its end.
- Small-hole rule: the pierce stays at the centre and there is no lead-out. A start pick sets where the straight lead-in meets the hole. An exit pick sets where the torch goes off. It must be at or past the overburn.
- Each contour without a pick keeps its automatic seam.
- A pick that a law cannot hold is refused by name. It is never moved. The text names the role and the point:
  - a pick farther than 1.5 kerf widths from each closed profile;
  - a pick when the operation has open runs only;
  - a lead-in or a lead-out with no room beside the part at the pick (the pierce or the torch off would be on the part);
  - a small-hole lead-in from the centre that would cross the part;
  - a small-hole exit pick inside the overburn;
  - an exit pick with control compensation (G41/G42), at the command door and in the generator.
- The kerf law and the cover law still judge the complete path.
- New generator door: `camcraft_motion::plasma::plasma_profile_picked`. `plasma_profile` calls it with no pick.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Plasma Profile. The command refused each pick on the kind. The generator always chose the seam (`longest_mid`, or the point nearest the centre for a small hole).

## Where the issue is silent (smallest change taken)

- Which contour takes a pick: the closed contour whose profile is nearest. The reach is 1.5 kerf widths (the 2D contour uses 1.5 tool diameters).
- How the cut gets to the exit: a run past the start in the cut direction. The stretch between the start and the exit is cut two times. A note on the path gives its length.
- "After the overburn": only the small-hole rule has an overburn. There the exit must be at or past it. A contour with leads has no overburn, so the exit pick alone sets the run.
- An exit pick with G41/G42 is refused by name. The programmed contour ends at its start, and a longer one needs a new proof of the compensation span. Mutation M2 showed that the generator emits a path without that refusal.
- Waterjet: `WaterjetProfile` is on `main` now, with its own planner and tabs. This PR does not change it. A pick on it is still refused by name. The slice is #3983.
- UI: this PR changes no UI file. The operation page reads `KindInfo::pick()`.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/3334-plasma-start-exit.md`.

## Merge refresh and final validation

Final head: `1c5dce3386d3289800903f9181334a9c88869b55`.
Current upstream main merged: `aef12fea67e0082e7ba835a3d9fcade8e2c11eb0`.

Class: DELTA. The merge has three hand-resolved additive hunks:

- `operation/pick_kinds.rs`: keep Plasma Profile `Ring` and `Thread | Drill | Bore` `HoleOrder` arms.
- `tests/start_exit_shared.rs`: keep both `plasma` and `hole_order` modules.
- `tests/start_exit_shared.rs`: keep both plasma and hole-order capability checks.

Wire exit refusal, Slot, turning and 5-axis contour entries stay present. Main's MCP tools and UI start/exit lists remain intact. Their diff against main is empty. No other code changed in this refresh.

All commands below ran on the final merge head, against the base above.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 765 steps; 0 failed; 0 stalled; 7923 tests passed; 98 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | passed |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | 110 steps; 0 failed; 0 stalled; includes 109 reached targets and their release build |
| app `start_exit_shared` | 28 passed: includes plasma, drilling hole order, turning and 5-axis contour |
| app `slot_start_exit` | 10 passed |
| app `wire_dxf_selection` | 14 passed: includes named arc exit refusal |
| app `mcp_wire_contour` / `mcp_plasma` | 10 / 6 passed |
| motion library | 706 passed; 22 ignored; includes all nine `plasma::picks_tests` |
| app `golden_cl` | 34 passed |
| app `example_catalog` | 43 passed; 4 ignored in debug; all 4 ignored cases passed in heavy |
| app `example_catalog_adaptive` / `example_catalog_edge_work` | 1 / 1 passed |

Pin proof on this merge: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick`.

- Replace the plasma `Ring` arm with `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)`: RED, one assertion failure at `start_exit_shared.rs:79`. Restore: GREEN, one passed.
- Replace the drilling `HoleOrder` arm with `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)`: RED, one assertion failure at `start_exit_shared.rs:81`. Restore: GREEN, one passed.

body:
Add the **Mikron WF3 DCM (LinuxCNC)** shipped machine definition from `paulsvc/linuxcnc-mill2-config` (`mill2.ini` and README).

- Added [assets/machines/mikron-wf3-dcm-linuxcnc.mch](assets/machines/mikron-wf3-dcm-linuxcnc.mch):
  - 3-axis mill (`vendor: "Camcraft"`, `model: "Mikron WF3 DCM (LinuxCNC)"`, `kind: "mill"`), metric (`mm`, `degrees`).

title: fix(ui): the tool window's next tool number skips reserved pockets; the full-probe refusal says what to do
body:
## What changed

Three items from the delta safety read of PR #3284 (#2604):

1. **The tool window's next number.** When you add a tool, the window compares the typed number with the number `AddTool` will give, and queues `SetToolNumber` only when they differ. The window used `tool_numbers::next_free`, which ignores the machine's reserved pockets. With T1 reserved for a probe, a typed 1 queued nothing, and the cutter became T2 with no message. A new function, `tool_numbers::next_free_for`, calls the same allocation as `AddTool` (`tool_reservations::allocate`), and the window uses it. Now a typed 1 goes to `SetToolNumber`, which refuses it by name.
2. **Every probe pocket is full.** A new probe is still refused (a probe in an ordinary pocket can break the control's probe macros). The refusal now names the pockets and says what to do:
   `tool 'Probe 2': the probe pockets of <model> (T1) all hold a tool. Delete or renumber the tool in one of these pockets, or reserve one more probe pocket in the machine file`
3. **Plain words.** A refusal names a `tool_setter` reservation as "tool setter", in the app and in the post check of the tool stream. The word "probe" does not change, so the tests and agents that match on it still match.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3667-tool-reservations.md`.

## How tested

- New app tests in `crates/app/tests/tool_reservations.rs`: `next_free_for_a_new_tool_matches_add_tool`, `a_probe_with_every_probe_pocket_full_says_what_to_do`, `a_tool_setter_pocket_is_named_in_plain_words`.
- New UI test `egui_app::tool_number_tests::a_new_tools_typed_number_is_compared_with_the_reserved_aware_allocation`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- `cargo xtask gate quick`: 29 of 29 steps pass.

## Not exercised

The Add tool button in the desktop app was not clicked. The UI test calls the same function that the button calls.

Changelog: The tool window now expects the same tool number that Add tool gives on a machine with reserved pockets, and a full set of probe pockets gets a refusal that says what to do.
Effort: low

title: DXF import: MPOLYGON and 3D surface records hidden in a non-drawing section are refused, not dropped
body:
## What changed

The DXF reader skips the sections that carry no geometry (CLASSES, ACDSDATA, THUMBNAILIMAGE) and refuses a file when a drawable record sits in one of them, so nothing is dropped silently. It knows a record is drawable from `ENTITY_KINDS` in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/entities.rs`. That list lacked `MPOLYGON` and the six SURFACE subtypes (`EXTRUDEDSURFACE`, `LOFTEDSURFACE`, `NURBSURFACE`, `PLANESURFACE`, `REVOLVEDSURFACE`, `SWEPTSURFACE`). They are on the list now (46 to 53 names).

`SUN` stays off the list on purpose. It is in the ENTITIES chapter of the DXF Reference, but AutoCAD writes it in OBJECTS (subclass `AcDbSun`, no `AcDbEntity`), and the OBJECTS reader refuses every kind on this list as "graphical entity in OBJECTS". Adding it would refuse real AutoCAD files with sun settings. A comment above the list says so.

## How tested

- New `dxf_classes_section::mpolygon_and_the_surface_kinds_in_a_section_without_geometry_are_refused`: each of the seven kinds in each of the three inert sections is a named refusal. It fails without the change.
- New `dxf_objects_section::a_sun_object_in_objects_stays_inert`: a SUN object in OBJECTS imports the same entities as the file without it.
- All DXF suites pass (`dxf`, `dxf_classes_section`, `dxf_objects_section`, `dxf_inert_sections`, `dxf_refusals`).
- `cargo xtask gate quick` on Windows: 1203 of 1206 steps pass, clippy clean. The three failures do not touch DXF and come from this checkout: `sinumerik_810m_post::air_cut_kit_posts_cleanly_and_matches_committed_kit` (the golden `.mpf` was checked out with CRLF line endings), `catalog_render::catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly` (`rough-finish`: "its file changed", the same line-ending cause) and `egui_app` (the test binary stops with an access violation, a GPU driver crash here).

## Not exercised

No real DXF file with MPOLYGON or a surface record in an inert section was opened; the tests use synthetic records.

Changelog: DXF import refuses a damaged file that hides an MPOLYGON or 3D surface record in a section without geometry, instead of dropping it silently.
Effort: low

title: fix(mcp): warn at add_tool when the tool's speed is outside the machine's spindle range
body:
## What changed

- `add_tool` (MCP) now returns a `warning` when the speed of the new tool is outside the spindle range of the mounted machine. Example: `EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the Tormach 770MX (ML)'s 10000 - the post will be held; set the tool's speed (edit_tool) or apply_cutting_data`.
- The UI shows the same text in the status line when a tool is added. The text comes after the holder note.
- The problem line of the machine check for an operation now names the fix: `Face1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs 12000 rpm, above the machine's 10000 - set the tool's speed (edit_tool) or apply_cutting_data`. The check of the default machine (#2321) uses the same words.
- The add does not change the speed of the tool. The machine check, the post gate and the posted G-code do not change.
- A finding for an NC line (`SourceLocation::NcLine`) keeps its old text. A posted NC file has no document tool to edit.
- The schema text of `add_tool` describes the new `warning` key.

Code:

- `crates/post/src/machine/check.rs`: the constant `SPINDLE_FIX`, the function `spindle_range_warning`, and one shared range test for the check and the warning.
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs`: `AddTool::with_holder` reads the mounted machine and keeps the warning. `AddTool::warning()` returns it.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`: the reply key `warning`. The file stays at 412 lines.
- `crates/app/src/posting_default_machine.rs`: the same fix words.
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: the status line.

## Cause

Only the add of a tool took the catalog speed without a reading of the mounted machine. `apply_cutting_data` and the Feeds tab spindle row already say when the machine holds a speed. Thus the first word came from the machine check at verify, after the work was generated. That line did not name a fix.

## Tests

Pins:

- `crates/app/tests/mcp/add_tool_spindle_warning.rs` (in the `mcp` directory suite, no new test binary):
  - `add_tool_warns_of_a_speed_above_the_mounted_machine`
  - `add_tool_warns_of_a_speed_below_the_mounted_machine`
  - `add_tool_does_not_warn_inside_the_range_or_without_a_machine`
  - `verify_still_holds_the_post_and_names_the_fix`
- `crates/ui/tests/machine.rs`: `adding_a_tool_above_the_machines_speed_says_so_in_the_status`
- `crates/post/tests/machine_check.rs`: `pure_tool_checks_keep_rpm_sizes_and_distinct_tool_count` (expected text extended)
- `crates/app/tests/default_machine_limits.rs`: `no_mounted_machine_is_refused_above_the_default_spindle_maximum` (expected text extended)

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code the "above", "below" and "verify" pins failed. The reply had no `warning` (`left: Null`), and the verify line ended at `above the machine's 10000`.

Mutation results (each mutation was made, the pin ran red, the code was restored, the pin ran green):

| Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|
| `add_tool` reply drops the warning (`mcp/edit.rs`) | the "above" and "below" pins |
| `AddTool::with_holder` computes no warning (`commands/tool.rs`) | the "above" and "below" pins, the UI pin |
| The machine check adds no fix (`machine/check.rs`) | the "verify" pin, `pure_tool_checks_keep_rpm_sizes_and_distinct_tool_count` |
| The old `posting_default_machine.rs` from `upstream/main` | `no_mounted_machine_is_refused_above_the_default_spindle_maximum` |
| The UI status drops the warning (`state.rs`) | the UI pin |

Three mutations were hand edits, not a copy of the old file. The old `mcp/edit.rs`, `commands/tool.rs` and `machine/check.rs` do not compile against the new callers.

Final checks for the screenshot review round (2026-11-25):

PR head: `7d4686af9528267a7f966ed1a307b27c4cb1779c`. No source commit was needed for this finding.

Current fetched base: `upstream/main` at `10ea81a2a1da2f883d43385757db802e83c99fd1`.

| Command or check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | RED. 377 executed steps: 376 passed, 1 failed, 0 stalled. The failed UI build skipped 15 UI suite steps. Wall time: 24.5 minutes. |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | RED. 67 steps: 66 passed, 1 failed, 0 stalled. Wall time: 31.6 minutes. |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | GREEN. |
| `app suites: example_catalog` | 43 passed, 4 ignored. |
| `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive` | 1 passed. |
| `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work` | 1 passed. |
| `app suites: solid_law_goldens` | 7 passed. |
| `app suites: mcp` | 54 passed. |
| UI status pin, with warning temporarily removed | RED. The status contained no spindle warning. |
| UI status pin, after restoration | GREEN. 1 passed. |
| Temporary shipping-layout capture test, before and after | GREEN. Both screenshots rendered with software Vulkan. |

The UI status pin is `adding_a_tool_above_the_machines_speed_says_so_in_the_status`.
The mutation removed only `.chain(command.warning())` from the UI status assembly.
The source was restored exactly after the RED run. The restored pin passed.
All temporary capture source was removed before the gates. The worktree is clean.

Quick failed during `ui build (--no-run)` with `E0463: can't find crate for camcraft_cl` at `crates/app/src/lib.rs:7:9`.
The errors also named `camcraft_geometry`, `camcraft_tools`, `camcraft_motion`, `camcraft_sim`, and `camcraft_post`.
The build reported 331 errors. A narrower retry and a retry without sccache failed with the same errors.
No cause was established. No build configuration or source was changed to address these errors.

Heavy failed in `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`.
The test was `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.
Its mesh assertion at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:80` reported `left: 5232`, `right: 6228`.
This round did not change that test or its source. The failure was not checked on bare upstream/main.

## Goldens moved

None in this PR or this review round. The three catalog suites and `solid_law_goldens` ran and passed.
`git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD -- '*.nc' '*.cl' examples/catalog` is empty.
The current upstream branch has separate catalog changes; this PR does not include those changes.

## UI evidence

Both images show the catalog add of `EM-0300-2FL` with `Tormach 770MX (ML)` mounted. The tool keeps 15000 rpm.

The temporary test harness used the shipping shell layout and clicked the catalog Add button. The capture used software Vulkan.

Before: the UI warning was temporarily removed from the status assembly. The status contains the holder note.

![Before: catalog add without the spindle warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/a8a13408bfcea24c4dcd205f99e1b1bf6b19a064/pr-3963/catalog-add-before.png)

After: the unchanged PR head shows the 15000 rpm / 10000 rpm warning and the suggested actions.

![After: catalog add shows the spindle warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/a8a13408bfcea24c4dcd205f99e1b1bf6b19a064/pr-3963/catalog-add-after.png)

The images are stored only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch at `a8a13408bfcea24c4dcd205f99e1b1bf6b19a064`. No capture source or images were added to the PR branch.

## Not exercised

- The 15 UI suite steps skipped after the UI build failure. The capture test and status pin ran before the gates.
- A bare upstream replay of the gate failures. Their cause and regression status are not established.
- The light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`). I did not run it. The review runs it on the final head.
- A lathe machine and the tool-library import path. They use the same command and the same function.

## Overlaps

- #3946 (`feat(tools)`, `needs-rework`) changes one line in the same function, `add_tool` in `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` (the `definition` branch, line 241). This PR changes the reply lines of that function (lines 269-279). The hunks are 28 lines apart and merge without a conflict. I did not stack on #3946: it is a 56-file `feat` that merges at a cut, and a stack would hold this fix until then. #3946 also changes `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, in a different hunk (line 31; this PR changes line 343). The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #3251 changes other functions in `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` (`patched`, `opt_in_kept`). It touches the same file, different functions. The PR that merges second refreshes.

title: feat(ui): add, move and remove the axes of a machine in the file editor
body:
The Machines pane's file editor gets an "Axis chain" group. The group adds, moves and removes the axis parts of a `.mch` file, reverses a linear axis, and sets the direction of a rotary axis. The editor changes the file's own JSON, so it keeps every key that it does not know. The decisions and the open questions are in `docs/decisions/2756-machine-axis-chain.md`.

**Before** (v0.26.0): the file editor of the same grblHAL 3-axis machine, with no Axis chain group above General.

![Before: the Machines file editor in v0.26.0, General first and no Axis chain group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2756/axis-chain-before.png)

**After** (this PR): the Axis chain group above General.

![After: the Axis chain group on the same 3-axis mill, above General](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2756/axis-chain.png)

## What changed

- **`MachineDraft`** (`crates/app/src/machine/chain.rs`, `draft.rs`) adds, moves and removes axis parts in `kinematics.default.parts`, like `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant`. A refused edit changes nothing. The validator judges the result as before.
  - A new axis goes **on the table** (beside the table's axes, before the head; a rotary there turns the work) or **carries the head** (it takes the head's slot; a rotary there tilts the tool).
  - **Remove** keeps what the axis carried: its `parts` take its place, in order. Its controller row goes with it.
  - **Up and Down** trade an axis with its neighbour row. The tree keeps its shape, so a move never changes which slot carries the head. An axis keeps all its own keys (`pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, `sign_convention`, unknown keys) and gets the `parent` and `chain_order` (#1962) of its new slot.
  - A move trades only with an axis of the same kind (rotary or linear) that moves the same thing (the work or the tool). Other moves are refused, and the refusal says to remove the axis and add it again.
  - A linear is reversed with `"direction": -1` (#373). Back to standard removes the key.
  - A rotary's `axis` is ±X, ±Y, ±Z or three numbers. The editor suggests the RS-274 letter (about X is A, about Y is B, about Z is C) and adds a note to a row whose letter does not agree. It does not refuse it.
- **The validator** keys the work-length refusals by axis and key (`A nose_to_axis`, `work_length_refusals` in `crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs`), so each refusal shows at its row and not above the grid. The rule is the parser's own rule.
- **The editor rows** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/machine_axis_chain.rs`) draw in one property grid, like General and the editor's other groups (`prop_grid` in `layout/form.rs`, #1122): one setting per row, the label in the first column and the control beside it, help as a hover text. A first version pushed the controls to the right edge (`prop_row`), so in a wide pane they drifted away from their labels. Each axis has a row with its letter and kind and the buttons Up, Down and ✖. Their accessible names are "Move A up", "Move A down" and "Remove A". The direction and the place of a new axis are dropdowns.
  - `nose_to_axis` (#804) and `axis_to_table` (#1107) are rows for a rotary that turns the work. A rotary that carries the head shows them only when the file states one, so that the user can clear it.
  - A row whose `offset` has no parent rotary gets a note (see Q1 below).
  - The fields have stable ids, so a note or a refusal that comes or goes above a field does not take the focus while the user types.
- **The rows are built once per edit** (the frame-cost rule, #2238). `MachineDraft::chain_view` (`crates/app/src/machine/chain_view.rs`) holds the rows, each row's notes and the refusal keys that show at a row. The draft is the file's one writer: `value` is now private, read with `value()`, and every write, `value_mut()` included, drops the view. A still frame reads it back. The group and the view are named `ui/machines.editor.axis_chain` and `ui/machines.editor.axis_chain.view` for the frame probe. The draft's `refusals()` and `groups()` still run on each frame, as on `main` before this PR. Five existing test lines read `value()` instead of the field.
- The Machines pane's editor and detail view fill the width of the pane.

The machine window ("edit a machine" from the Setup pane) also has "add axis". That window edits the mounted `Machine` (a flat list of axes and limits) through `EditMachineApply`. This group edits the axis tree of the `.mch` file and keeps the keys that the editor does not know. They are two different tools, and this PR does not change the machine window.

## Open questions (the decision file takes the recommended option)

The maintainer has not answered these yet. Each one has a cost to change in the decision file.

- **Q1** (comment of 2026-11-20): an `offset` on a rotary with no parent rotary. This PR shows a note at the row and does not refuse the file. We recommend a refusal in the validator.
- **Q2** (comment of 2026-11-20): a move trades only with an axis of the same kind. This PR also refuses a trade between an axis that moves the work and one that moves the tool.
- The three questions in the issue: the order with #1970, the #785 pair beside the #1962 pair, and a machine with a tilting head and a rotary table. This PR adds a head axis and a table axis to the same file, but does not draw a "Kinematics" group.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the tree of `e1ac7b786` (run just before the commit, nothing else changed): 124 steps, 0 failed, 6.6 min.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` on `e1ac7b786`: 4 steps, 0 failed, 5.3 min.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The gate's batch plan, run one step at a time, on `303188d61` (before the last merge of main): 1,073 steps. One red step was `a_kind_that_is_not_a_kind_refuses_at_the_door`, which main has since fixed ("router" is now a kind). The suite `machine` is green after the merge.
- No heavy step: the issue is `P6`, not `P1` under the safety floor.

## Pinning tests

34 new tests, none removed. The new app tests are modules of the existing `machine` suite (`crates/app/tests/machine/`), so this PR adds no test binary (#3187).

- `crates/app/tests/machine/axis_chain.rs` (15): add on the table and with the head, remove, move, the refusals, unknown keys kept, and `a_rotary_that_turns_the_work_never_trades_with_one_that_tilts_the_tool`.
- `crates/app/tests/machine/axis_rows.rs` (9): what each row says, the RS-274 letter note, the offset note, reverse, turn about, and the work lengths.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_axis_chain.rs` (7): the group through AccessKit labels: an A added on the table, moved and saved; a refused letter and a remove; X reversed and set back; a turn about Y that suggests B and a note for an A about Y; the FlexiHAL router built from a blank mill and saved; the offset note; and a field that keeps its focus when a refusal goes away.
- `crates/app/src/machine/chain_view.rs` (2): a read with no write between builds nothing; every write (add, move, turn, reverse, remove, a hand write through `value_mut`, a field elsewhere) gives the view a fresh build gives.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/frame_cost_caches.rs` (1): `the_axis_chain_is_built_once_per_edit_of_the_machine_file`. Still frames and typing in the form build nothing (the `chain_view_builds` counter); an added axis and a write to the JSON build it again, equal to a fresh build.
- Mutation probes on the cache, each restored after: a `clear` that drops nothing fails `every_write_gives_the_view_a_fresh_build_gives`, the cache test and `an_offset_with_no_parent_rotary_shows_a_note_at_its_row`; a memo that builds on every read fails `a_read_with_no_write_between_builds_nothing` and the cache test.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_edit.rs`: `pick_kind` scrolls the dropdown into view first, because the group makes the form taller.

## Not exercised

- The offset-note UI test was written after the note, so it was not seen red first.
- No output was posted from a machine file that this editor wrote. The values feed the clearance gates and the post kinematics through `parse_mch`, which the app tests check.
- The "Kinematics" group (`pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, `controller.rtcp` as fields) is #1970's. This PR keeps those keys on every edit and does not draw them.
- `validate.rs`, `egui_app/mod.rs`, `egui_app/tests.rs` and `tests/machine.rs` are over 400 lines on main. This PR adds 1, 1, 1 and 9 lines to them.

body:
What changed:
- `OpParams::Bore` has an `entry` field (plunge, ramp, helix). Plunge is the default and is
  not written to the project file.
- The links' approach `ramp_angle` and `helix_angle` cap every descent.
- A bore with entry ramp or helix may use up to 4096 ring-ramp legs (`MAX_BORE_ZIG_LEGS`). The

- Ø3.2 hole: worst descent 5.00 degrees (main: 6 axial dives).

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- The Sodick post refuses an open run's skims by name at its rapid
  guard: its manual states no such pass structure, and the generic ISO
  post is the one that cuts, travels and threads anew around each
  boundary.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

Screenshots (images only on the fork's pr-screenshots branch)

- Controls, before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-controls-before.png
- Controls, after (the new Closing overlap row and its help): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-controls-after.png
- Full window, before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-window-before.png
- Full window, after: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-window-after.png

Rework after the safety review (head 795d69e95)

The eight review items of 2026-11-25 are addressed on the same branch:

1. The Centre slit's run-out clearance joins the generation stamp
   (cutting.rs), so an edited or re-stated clearance reads Stale -
   pinned through the edit command and a project reload (wire_stamp).
2. The overlap's ride includes the seam edge's own remainder back to
   the seam: a 100 mm overlap covers exactly 100 mm of arc, forward
   and reversed, and a ride longer than one full lap is refused by
   name (motion tests, both directions, near the perimeter).
3. An open run's skim passes are rethreaded in the air: a travel move
   (a rapid, no wire through it) marks each pass boundary, the wire
   verify judges each pass at its own kerf and its own ends, and the
   generic ISO post cuts, travels and threads anew around it - a new
   app test generates, verifies AND posts an open run with a skim
   (new golden wire_contour_open_skims.nc).
4. A stated overlap beside a no-core burnout is refused by name at the
   command door (create and edit tested).
5. A stated overlap on a 4-axis cut and beside a constant taper is
   refused by name at the command door (the 3-degree/1 mm case that
   once failed with "repeats a point" now refuses at the door;
   create and edit tested per combination).
6. The three-file merge with current main keeps both sides; the
   resolved tree builds and its gates run (below).
7. Before / after screenshots of the changed Wire Contour controls
   are on the fork's pr-screenshots branch and linked below.
8. This PR edits .claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md; the body
   carries the process line. PROCESS_VERSION is untouched.

The choice per item is recorded in
docs/decisions/3216-wire-overlap-rework.md: items 2 and 3 are defects
of what the feature claims, so they are implemented properly; items 4
and 5 are refused by name at the command door, safer than a
half-implemented overlap on the burnout, 4-axis and taper builders.

Main moved while the rework ran (the wire exit pick, the arc joins, the rotary stated axis, the tool preview), so the branch carries one more merge of current main, resolved keeping both sides, and the gates below ran on the refreshed head.

Gates on the resolved tree: motion lib 668 passed, sim lib 253 passed, app lib 311 passed, ui lib 1659 passed; mcp_wire_contour 8, wire_verify 3, golden_cl 34, wire_post 13, wire_stamp 8, wire_contour 19, wire_burnout 4, wire_taper 11, wire_4axis 8, wire_verify_tol 4,
conformance 7 (every builtin posts every golden byte exact), the
sodick wire suites, g_edm_post, agie_native; clippy app + motion + sim
+ ui --all-targets -D warnings clean. example_catalog's
2d/drill-overfeed refusal.txt CRLF red is the known environmental
#3628, unrelated to this diff (41 of its steps pass).

Changelog: Wire Contour: a stated closing overlap rides the cut past its seam; a centre-line slit side for open runs; skim passes on open runs re-entered from the air.

fork synced at v0.25.0

Process change: yes

Fixes #3216

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
  - A helix inside the uncut core of a tool that is not centre-cutting (review finding on 4bd091166). The core is `plunge_law::CORE` of the tool radius. The wall circle must stand at least that far off the hole axis (`rc >= CORE * r`). The message names the helix radius, the uncut core and the smallest hole that the tool helixes (Ø9 for a Ø6 tool with no leave). A centre-cutting tool keeps the small helix.
- Pass starts at (#3360, from `main`) on a Helical Bore: one helix for each hole has no ring order. Inside and Outside are refused by name at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The Passes tab shows the refusal under the row. Auto is unchanged.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
  - `a_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_of_a_non_centre_cutting_tool_is_refused`: the review's case (Ø6.5, Ø6 tool, 0.4 mm per turn, helix radius 0.25 mm). The NC tool is refused with "1.500 mm uncut core" and "9.000 mm". Ø9 and the issue's Ø11 counterbore still helix with that tool.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_pass_order_by_name`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `a_small_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_is_refused_through_the_operation`: the review's probe through `operation::generate`. The NC tool is refused; the CC tool keeps the small helix with no plunge.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_pass_order_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator both refuse it.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::a_helical_bore_says_the_pass_start_refusal` (ui lib): Rings take the order; Helical shows the refusal line.

## Gates

All gates ran on the final head 6932f4022. This head adds the core fix (c85bdd982) and merges `upstream/main` four times, the last at 33597a2fb. Each conflict was resolved by keeping the two sides:

- d5fafe8be (main at 6cfc0a6d4): #3360 added Pass starts at to Bore. The Bore records, the project file, the stamp, the params patch, the generator and the Passes tab now carry both `strategy` and `pass_start` (13 files; `git show --remerge-diff d5fafe8be`). The three Bore test literals get the other field.
- 7ae8b1532 (main at 01e177bf5): two mod lines in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`.
- 88f7fc420 (main at 81365c33b): two new tests side by side in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/pass_start.rs` (main's #3745 test and the helical pass-start test).
- 6932f4022 (main at 33597a2fb): no conflict.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 809 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (108.3 min). It includes `motion suites: bore_helix`, `motion suites: bore_pass_start`, `app suites: bore_helical`, `app suites: bore_pass_start` and `ui suites: lib`.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets` on `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean (on the merge 88f7fc420; the last merge brought only main's commits and no conflict).
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 104 steps, 1 failed (63.6 min). The known-fail steps are red as expected.
  - The red step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. It fails at `pocket3d_hsm.rs:79`: the STEP mesh of `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` has 5232 facets, and the pin is 6228. This test is a 3D Pocket and does not use the Bore operation. `Cargo.lock`, `crates/kernel` and `testdata` are the same as `main`. #3886 reports this step red on `main`.
- An earlier quick gate on 88f7fc420 (merge of `main` at 81365c33b) had 809 steps and 1 failed step, `app suites: plunge_depth_tab`. That `main` had #3866 and #3679 without the re-pin of #3927. The merge of 33597a2fb brought #3927, and the step is green on the final head.

## Screenshots

The Bore operation page, rendered by the UI test harness (`egui_kittest`) from a real Bore operation.

| | Rings | Helical |
|---|---|---|
| Passes tab | ![Passes, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-rings.png) | ![Passes, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-helical.png) |
| Heights tab | ![Heights, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-rings.png) | ![Heights, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-helical.png) |

- Passes tab: the Strategy combo shows the two strategies. The Spring pass check shows only for Helical.
- Heights tab: the last Levels row is "Stepdown" for Rings and "Helix pitch" for Helical.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A tool that is not centre-cutting helixes only when the helix clears its uncut core. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.
- The screenshots show the head 4bd091166. The new refusal line under Pass starts at is pinned by the UI test, not by a screenshot.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.
